messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the authn/authz sync — RFC said we should pick between permission-derivation (compute effective perms from role + project membership at runtime) vs role-shadowing (materialize a role snapshot on the service token). open to opinions, tradeoffs, ops costs?
arch-bot: RFC: https://redwood/rfcs/2026/perm-derivation-vs-shadowing (posted) :link:
sam: my gut: derivation is cleaner conceptually, single source of truth. but worried about latencies and consistency when services call other services (chained calls).
jordan: +1 on the consistency concern. derivation means we need a very fast authz cache or per-request evals become expensive. also harder to reason about when you rotate roles. :thinking:
lee: role-shadowing avoids a bunch of runtime checks — you hand a service token a concrete set of permissions and downstream services just check the token. simpler fast path. downside: stale permissions if role changes and you don't refresh shadows.
maria: exactly. two main vectors: 1) runtime cost & complexity (derivation) 2) stale divergence & lifecycle (shadowing). also migration cost for existing API keys.
sam: question: can we do hybrid? derive for user API keys (short-lived) and shadow for long-lived service tokens? that feels pragmatic.
jordan: hybrid seems reasonable. propose rules: - short-lived api keys (<=24h) -> derive - long-lived service tokens -> shadow, with automated shadow refresh on role change or token rotation events
lee: agree but need fallback semantics. what if shadow refresh fails? forced deny or fall back to old shadow? we should prefer fail-safe (deny) but that causes availability issues.
maria: maybe use "grace window" semantics: when role changes, we issue new shadow asynchronously; old shadows remain valid for X minutes (configurable by team). operations can override per-org.
auditor-bot: note: auditors prefer derivation for auditability because there's single source of truth; with shadowing we need to persist snapshots for historical audit. :memo:
jordan: we can store shadow snapshot metadata in the audit log when we mint the token. that gives historical context without recomputing past state. e.g. store `{token_id, roles_at_mint, project_ids}` as part of token record.
lee: implementation sketch: shadow tokens carry a compressed permission bitmap + `shadow_version`. on incoming request, service verifies token signature + checks permission bits. shadow refresh pipeline listens to role-change events and re-mints shadows asynchronously. if re-mint fails, increment `failed_refresh_count` metric and page after N.
maria: sample token payload (simplified):
```
{
  "sub": "svc:billing",
  "typ": "service_token",
  "shadow_version": 42,
  "perms": ["billing.read","billing.write"],
  "projects": ["proj:123"]
}
```
sam: for derivation path we need a hot cache: key is `(subject_id, project_id, role_version)` and TTL ~10s? also ability to bulk-warm cache on deploys. have we measured perf impact?
maria: infra: we can add a sidecar auth-cache (local LRU + async refresh from central policy store). should be fine for 95th perc latency. we'll need to budget for extra ops.
jordan: corner case: cross-project delegation (service in proj A acting on proj B). derivation helps because you can compute intersection easily, shadowing forces us to include all delegated perms in shadow. that's OK but increases shadow payload size.
lee: also consider emergency revoke: if a key is compromised, shadowing requires invalidation store (revocation list) or short shadow TTLs. derivation can pick up denies immediately if role change is propagated.
maria: proposal: hybrid default + guardrails:
- default: user tokens -> derive, service tokens -> shadow
- shadow TTL default 1h, configurable per-org/service
- on critical revoke, push revocation to revocation-list + force shadow_version bump so old shadows fail after grace window
- persist snapshot metadata for auditability
- implement local auth-cache for derivation to meet latency SLOs
lee: sounds solid. who's owning the proto + rollout? I can take the shadow pipeline + revocation infra.
sam: I can own the derivation cache + policy store perf work.
jordan: I'll draft the implementation RFC and include migration steps + metrics (staleness, refresh-failures, cache-hit-rate, revoke-latency).
maria: perfect. let's sync on an RFC draft by EOD Fri. owners: @lee owns shadow infra, @sam owns derivation cache, @jordan owns RFC. I'll coordinate migration QA with platform. :+1:
auditor-bot: created ticket AUD-2026-317 for audit requirements, and TICKET-7881 for revocation infra.
arch-bot: noted — added owners to RFC tracker and slotted a follow-up sync next Tue 10am.
maria: thanks everyone. short follow-up: include a minimal compatibility shim so existing API keys keep working during migration (proxy applies old semantics).
sam: good call. I'll add a shim plan to my section.
maria: closing thread, will post RFC link once jordan's draft is ready. :wave:
